newsitem.title: CHINA: China punishes 12 banks, brokerages in share case.
newsitem.headline: China punishes 12 banks, brokerages in share case.

text.p: The China Securities Regulatory Commission has fined 12 bank branches and brokerages for illegally bidding for shares on credit, the China Securities newspaper reported on Saturday.
Such bidding is outlawed by Chinese securities regulations, which strictly ban any kind of stock trading on credit.
Analysts said it was the largest number of financial institutions publicly punished at the same time for this offence.

The CSRC imposed a fine of 1.13 million yuan on the Jiangmen branch of the Guangdong Development Bank for using 568.94 million yuan on August 30 to bid for shares of Qinghai Mingjiao, which listed local currency shares on the Shenzhen stock market, the newspaper said.

It imposed a fine of 790,000 yuan on the Zhongshan Securities Company for bidding 398.12 million yuan on August 27 for shares of Jiangsu Supu, which listed local currency shares on the Shanghai stock market.
The newspaper said it also imposed a fine of 690,000 yuan on Hainan Gangao International Trust and Investment for bidding 343.5 million yuan on August 30 for shares of Qinghai Mingjiao.
